detail.longDescription: arXiv:2611.33727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Global aging makes digital technology important for older adults healthy aging, yet graphical user interfaces remain inaccessible to many. Voice agents based on large language models may help, but users needs and reasons for sustained use remain unclear. We developed a phone-call-style companion that initiates conversations proactively and structures calls using a persona, conversation rules, and prior-call memory (facts, insights, relationship background). We conducted a two-week mixed-methods field study with 33 community-dwelling Korean older adults (29 women; aged 67-91), collecting call logs, pre-post questionnaires, and interviews. Participants made 608 calls following a daily-use recommendation; 25 continued afterward despite turn-taking difficulties. Loneliness and depression scores decreased significantly; among loneliness subfactors, only isolation (emotional loneliness) decreased significantly. Participants disclosed concerns withheld from family and linked companionship to being addressed by name, being remembered, and experiencing emotional reciprocity. We propose personalized conversation rules, accessible interaction, and user control over frequency and topics.
